sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9: ss.6-9 (incorporation), s.15.1 (unlimited liability corporation), s.25 (consideration for shares), s.101 (registered office), ss.106-110 (directors), s.161 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; Corporate Online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation - Form 5 under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, including the unlimited liability declaration under s.15.1
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under the ABCA. Shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine (s.25). For a ULC, unlimited shareholder liability supplements creditor protection in lieu of minimum capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation issue 100 common shares to the subscriber named in the Subscription Agreement in consideration of CAD 100; no statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the ABCA. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at Suite 1200, 333 Seventh Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta, and that the first directors be confirmed. RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, with authorization to open bank accounts, execute LME warrant transfers, and sign documentary letters of credit for wholesale copper cathode transactions. RESOLVED, that the officers implement all CRA tax registrations, municipal licensing, and regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via Service Alberta-accredited NUANS search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed name 'ABC Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ABC ULC' to verify distinctiveness; review the conflict report; after passing the search, file a Name Reservation Request to reserve the name for up to 90 days; obtain a written consent from any conflicting registered name holder if a cross-company similarity requires a co-existence letter.
required_dossiers: Signed authorization letter from proposed incorporators
Consent/co-existence letter from prior name holder (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on distinctiveness or confusion grounds, file a new NUANS search on an alternate name within the 90-day reservation window, or submit a documented co-existence consent and request re-adjudication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation (Form 5)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry pre-filing compliance unit / authorized corporate law practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 5 setting out the corporate name with the 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' designation, registered office address (Calgary), share structure (unlimited Common Shares without par value), first directors (minimum one; at least 25% resident Canadians, or at least one resident Canadian if fewer than four directors), and the express designation under s.15.1 ABCA of unlimited liability of shareholders. Have each incorporator execute the Articles and each director execute a signed consent to act.
required_dossiers: Registered office address confirmation and owner's consent (Form for registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry pre-filing screen rejects the documents due to technical defects, correct the identified schedules, re-execute the consent pages, and resubmit with a cover letter specifying the amendments made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with Alberta Corporate Registry and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Online portal or courier submission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Form 5 electronically through the Corporate Online portal or by physical courier to the Alberta Corporate Registry; pay the statutory filing fee (CAD 200 online plus NUANS fee); upon substantive review, receive the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique Alberta Corporation Access Number (CAN).
required_dossiers: Order to convey address / expedited handling request (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a rejection notice, file an Amending Articles (s.29 ABCA) for substantive corrections or submit a Declaration of Correction for typographical errors within 30 days to preserve the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance: Minute Book, Bylaws, Share Issuance, and Initial Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate secretary / legal counsel; Alberta Corporate Registry for subsequent change filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the corporate minute book at the registered office; adopt standard or bespoke bylaws; convene the first board meeting and pass the first board resolution; issue share certificates to subscribers; open corporate bank account; file the first Annual Return within 60 days of incorporation and, if the registered office or directors change, file the Notice of Change of Registered Office and Notice of Change of Directors forms with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: Bylaws (Form 1 initial bylaws or bespoke bylaws)
First board meeting minutes and resolutions
Share subscription agreement and issued share certificates
Registered office/notice of directors forms (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a post-incorporation filing is queried, pass a correcting board resolution and re-file the affected notice within the statutory cure period; late annual returns incur stabilization fees and can be remediated by expedited filing with payment of the prescribed late fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Alberta Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts: GST/HST (RT), corporate income tax (RC), payroll (RP) if staff are hired, and import/export (RM) account for cross-border LME copper cathode transactions; register with TRA for Alberta corporate income tax; if employees are engaged, register with the Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account details or pre-account confirmation letter
Commodity transaction description for import/export account (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or TRA suspends the registration pending verification, submit a certified corporate registry extract (Certificate of Status), director KYC documents, and a letter of explanation; escalate via the CRA Business Window service for manual clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Clearance for Wholesale Metals Trading
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality business licensing office (e.g., City of Calgary); Alberta Municipal Affairs for building occupancy; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for environmental screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal General Business Licence covering wholesale merchant distribution of non-ferrous metals; if warehousing copper cathodes or repacking, obtain a building occupancy permit, fire code inspection certificate, and confirm zoning compliance; verify that ISIC 4662 does not appear on Alberta's provincially regulated licensed occupations register; secure any landlord consent for hazardous material storage declarations if cathode weight exceeds structural thresholds.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and CRA BN confirmation
Lease agreement and zoning compliance letter
Fire code inspection certificate for the premises
Building structural load confirmation for cathode storage racks
Registration extract from Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality denies licensing due to zoning or use restrictions, apply for a discretionary use permit before the City Development Appeal Board or relocate to an industrial/commercial zone with permitted wholesale use.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Calgary / City of Edmonton Business Licensing Division (municipal); Alberta Municipal Affairs for building occupancy; no provincial industrial manufacturing licence is applicable to ISIC 4662 wholesale merchant distribution.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal General Business Licence (Business Licence under applicable municipal bylaw) plus CRA Import-Export Account (RM); mandatory for physical wholesale copper cathode operations and LME warrant settlement support.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Class 1: pure wholesale trading and warehousing of finished Grade A copper cathodes requires no Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Activity Registration; a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment may be required by commercial lenders for warehouse leases; registration under the Waste Control Regulation would apply only if copper scrap recovery or secondary materials processing is later added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater for trading-only activities; any sanitary or stormwater discharge must comply with the applicable municipal sewer and drainage bylaws (Alberta province-wide SEPP limits; City of Calgary sanitary sewer limits for copper and metals). Copper dust and fume occupational exposure to be maintained below ACGIH TLV-TWA of 1 mg/m3 (dust) and 0.1 mg/m3 (fume); packaging waste diverted pursuant to the Alberta Recycling Regulation; spill prevention and secondary containment plans required for any cathode warehousing area.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Code compliance certificate and municipal fire safety inspection; Alberta Building Code structural load clearance for cathode storage racks (dead/live load design per NBCC 2020); Occupational Health and Safety clearance under the Alberta OHS Act, including Hazardous Products Regulation SDS documentation, first-aid and emergency response plan, and workplace violence and harassment policy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - federal tax administration for corporate income tax and GST/HST; CRA portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (canada.ca). Alberta provincial corporate income tax is administered by the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA), Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act. Alberta ULC incorporation is filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta Registries), which coordinates CRA Business Number issuance. Export controls and export declarations are administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: S1: Incorporate the Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) through the Alberta Corporate Registry; obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, Corporate Access Number (CAN), registered office address in Alberta and Alberta registered agent. S2: Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) automatically via the registry-CRA integration, or file Form RC1 Request for a Business Number / use CRA Business Registration Online (BRO). S3: Activate CRA program accounts: RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RP (payroll if the ULC employs Canadian staff); all copper trading and invoicing activity should reference the RT account. S4: For foreign-controlled or non-resident-owned structures, provide the CRA with certified constating documents, proof of non-resident ownership, and a Canadian agent or representative for service; a non-resident GST/HST registrant without a permanent establishment in Canada may be required to post security. S5: Register for Alberta corporate income tax with the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (the T2 corporate return serves as the federal-provincial filing vehicle for the combined federal and Alberta corporate taxes). S6: Retain the BN certificate, program account confirmation letters and registration dates for counterparty KYC/AML due diligence on LME warrant transfers and documentary letter of credit trade lines.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (default); Pass_Through_Eligible via subsection 104(2) Income Tax Act (Canada) election. An Alberta ULC is by default a Canadian resident corporation and a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act, subject to federal corporate income tax at 15% plus Alberta corporate income tax at 8%, and to GST/HST registration as a single legal person. The entity is not in a territorial or tax-exempt zone regime. The default corporate classification can be displaced for Canadian tax purposes only by filing the subsection 104(2) ITA election, which deems the ULC not to be a corporation and deems each member to be a partner of a partnership, yielding full pass-through taxation and fiscal transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Subsection 104(2) Income Tax Act (Canada) election: the only mechanism available to convert the Alberta ULC's default entity-level taxation into pass-through treatment. The election is filed with the CRA by written notice (accompanied by the ULC board resolution and unanimous shareholder consent; no prescribed CRA form is assigned) and takes effect for the taxation year designated in the election. Upon a valid election, the ULC is deemed not to be a corporation, each member is deemed to be a partner of a partnership, and the members report their respective shares of income and are jointly and severally liable for GST/HST obligations; partnerships, not the ULC, become the GST/HST registrant. The election, once made, cannot be revoked without CRA consent. Hybrid mismatch and Canada-US tax treaty transparency rules (including treaty article IV(6) fiscally transparent entity provisions and BEPS Action 2) must be evaluated because the election may cause the ULC to be treated consistently or inconsistently with its US federal classification; no US Form 8832 check-the-box election has any effect on Canadian tax classification, and Canada does not offer any comparable check-the-box regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with prudential banking supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); foreign-exchange statistics and trade reporting administered through Statistics Canada and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada maintains no exchange-control approvals or licensing for ordinary cross-border payments, profit repatriation, or equity injections. Dividend and interest outflows remain subject to Canadian withholding taxes under the Income Tax Act and applicable tax treaties; no central bank permission is required for remittances. Anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance (Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act, FINTRAC) and international tax disclosure (FATCA/CRS, Part XVIII.1) apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Export receipts are not subject to any statutory surrender, conversion, or mandatory repatriation timeline. Settlement must be supported by normal commercial documentation (commercial invoice, bill of lading, customs entry summary). Export transactions are reportable to Statistics Canada under the Canadian Export Reporting framework and to the CBSA for customs clearance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium for use as a primary treasury account; offshore electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are not a recognized deposit-taking class in Canada. Any money-service business operating or soliciting clients in Canada must register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and comply with Canadian AML/CFT obligations. Unregistered offshore EMIs are legally constrained and will likely be rejected by Canadian chartered banks for correspondent settlement, particularly for LME warrant transfers and documentary LCs. An MSB-registered Canadian fintech may support ancillary payment aggregation but lacks the balance sheet capacity and SWIFT correspondent network necessary for high-value base-metals settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted under FINTRAC-compliant remote identification procedures using government-issued photo identification and third-party identity verification, but Canadian banks reserve the right to require a physical interview or a live verified video call for the entity's directors and ultimate beneficial owners, especially because copper cathode wholesale trading is categorized as Medium-Risk Enhanced. In practice, at least one director or senior authorized signatory with a Canadian presence or a Canadian nexus is required; the other non-resident directors can typically be onboarded via notarized identification, but the bank may mandate a live fintech-enabled video interview prior to activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC pass-through entity with unlimited liability and fractured ownership may mask true beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry certified extracts, certificate of incumbency, current register of directors and security holders, notarized UBO declarations, organizational chart, operating agreement and any unanimous shareholder agreement, tax election forms (e.g., section 216 election or treaty-based position), and audited or reviewed financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Metal trading and physical arbitrage volume trigger trade-based money-laundering red flags such as over/under-invoicing, use of transshipment corridors, or pricing inconsistent with LME quotations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master purchase and sale agreements, itemized commercial invoices linked to daily LME cash-settlement / official three-month prices, LME warrant or warehouse certificate evidence, independent inspector/surveyor reports, bills of lading and packing lists, CBSA customs entry summaries (B3 documents), proof of freight/insurance, and a treasury reconciliation of goods flow to cross-border payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners from a FATF-listed or sanctioned-monitored jurisdiction trigger heightened due-diligence and refusal risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds affidavits, certified passport copies and proof-of-address, tax residency certificates, institutional introductions/reference letters from a fully regulated financial institution in the owner's jurisdiction, and a board resolution disclosing all beneficial owners with confirmation of adverse-media screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement through third-party clearing agents or LC payment chains deviating from the primary sale contract may trigger bank rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated contractual chain from initial seller to intermediate trader to final end-buyer, UCP 600 compliant documentary credit terms and any amendments, the exact payment schedule and account designations, LME warrant transfer confirmations, and a written commercial rationale for any intermediary clearing account or direct-pay arrangement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections must be effected as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with a clear payment message referencing 'equity contribution' or 'additional paid-in capital' and the company's legal name. The underlying remittance should include a certified board resolution authorizing the issuance of shares; Canadian banks verify the remitter's identity and source of funds, and may require a copy of the share subscription agreement, proof of no issuance to a prohibited person, and notification under Part XVIII.1 (FATCA/CRS) where a non-resident 25% or greater beneficial holder exists. Payments settle through Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or a correspondent bank's CHF clearing channel, and funds become immediately available once nexus to the ULC is established.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement for copper cathode purchases/disbursements will primarily run through SWIFT MT103 for bulk wire transfers or through the trade-lending desk. A commercial documentary letter of credit (LC) issued by the Canadian bank under UCP 600 provides the payment rail against presentation of compliant shipping and LME warrant documents; for same-day and high-value CAD shipments, the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) is used; for foreign-currency disbursements, the Canadian bank's correspondent network, typically through New York (USD) and Frankfurt/London (EUR/GBP), executes the settlement. Additional liquidity may be raised via the ULC's committed credit facility and precious/base-metals advance lines secured against LME warrants.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNH)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market or restricted convertibility currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL, MXN)
Cross-currency swaps (FX and interest-rate swaps under ISDA/CSA master agreements)
Vanilla FX options (European-style) and exotic options acceptable under internal treasury policy
CME-listed FX futures and cleared FX swaps for exchange-traded hedges
FX price-at-risk (volume-optional) hedging through activation of margin lines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry Annual Return filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing is due on or before the sixtieth (60th) day after the corporation's anniversary date of registration/incorporation; the deadline recurs annually and is anchored to the original Alberta registration date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If filed after the 60-day window, a CAD 45 late penalty applies in addition to the CAD 60 filing fee; continued non-filing triggers a notice of failure to file from the Registrar and, if not remedied, administrative dissolution of the ULC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate income tax, including unlimited liability corporation schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta corporate tax is administered under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due six calendar months after each fiscal year-end, irrespective of the fiscal period chosen by the ULC; this is a nationwide CRA statutory deadline, not a corporate registry anniversary filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 5% penalty on the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month for late filing, increasing to 10% on repeated compliance failures; interest accrues daily on both tax and penalties, and the CRA may assess a delinquency based on the outstanding balance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) sets no revenue or asset-size audit threshold. A private corporation is required to appoint a licensed auditor unless all shareholders consent in writing each financial year to waive the audit requirement; distributing or public companies cannot waive. Institutional lenders or commodity-trading counterparties may contractually impose an audit regardless of statutory exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; privately held Canada-controlled ULCs may prepare financial statements under Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) or IFRS. If the ULC is consolidated by a US or other foreign parent, IFRS or parent-compliant GAAP with reconciliation is commonly adopted for the statutory audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not operate a provincial beneficial-ownership registry. For a ULC, the register of members is the authoritative unlimited-liability ownership record; any transfer of shares must be entered in the register before the transferee can exercise voting rights or receive dividends. The annual return to Alberta Corporate Registry is signed by a director or officer and constitutes the annual statutory confirmation that the registered office, directors, and corporate status information are current; ownership information is updated in the on-site register contemporaneously with transfers rather than through a separate annual UBO filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including share transfers and ownership records)
Register of Directors with statutory particulars and consent to act forms
Minute Book (directors' and shareholders' resolutions and meeting minutes)
General accounting records and documentation supporting the ULC's financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 220–550 USD per annum for registered office and registered agent services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000–18,000 USD per annum for a medium-risk physical copper cathode wholesaler, dependent on transaction volume and audit firm.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined regular corporate income tax rate (federal Part I tax of 15% after federal abatement and General Rate Reduction, plus Alberta corporate tax of 8%). The basic federal statutory rate is 38%, reduced by a 13% provincial abatement and a 13% General Rate Reduction for active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No copper wholesale tax holiday applies. Alberta applies a 2% small business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of taxable income for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations, but this is normally unavailable to a foreign-controlled Alberta ULC. Deductions include cost of goods sold for Grade A copper cathodes, carrying and storage costs, LME hedging losses, reasonable expenses under section 20, and treaty foreign tax credits. The ULC remains a Canadian taxpayer even where the shareholder has chosen transparent treatment for foreign tax purposes.
